title: Balanced Binary Tree
prompt:
Given the `root` of a binary tree, determine if it is height-balanced — meaning for every node in the tree, the heights of its left and right subtrees differ by no more than 1.

The tree is given as a level-order array where `null` marks a missing child (the standard LeetCode serialization). Your function receives this array directly; the starter code includes a helper that builds the tree from it, so you only need to implement the balance check.

examples.explanation: Every node's subtrees differ in height by at most 1.
The subtree rooted at the second node with value 2 has a left height of 2 and right height of 0, differing by more than 1.
An empty tree has no nodes to violate the balance condition, so it is trivially balanced.

constraints: The number of nodes is in the range [0, 5000]
hints: A naive approach recomputes height for every node from scratch, giving O(n^2) — think about how to avoid redundant recomputation.
Compute height and check balance in a single bottom-up (post-order) pass so each subtree's height is calculated only once.
Have the height helper return -1 as a sentinel the moment it detects an imbalance anywhere below, and propagate that -1 up immediately so the whole check short-circuits to false.

solution.approach: Do a single post-order DFS that returns the height of each subtree, but overload the return value: if a subtree is already found to be unbalanced, return -1 immediately as a sentinel instead of continuing to compute heights above it. At each node, if either child returns -1, or the two child heights differ by more than 1, propagate -1 upward. This computes the answer in one O(n) pass instead of recomputing heights repeatedly.
